fields.reasoning: In internal/workflow/builtin/ship-change.toml, ci-triage has two entry points, pr-green and rebased-green, both through on.fail, and no wait step feeds it directly. So 01M6XX4R8's rule finds nothing. Restarting at ci-triage itself is the current bug: it re-reads the head's stale ship-check state and fails in 1s (run 01M6XVTXGJAMQRBZKDZKY0Z01T, PR #393). Restarting at pr-green or rebased-green directly would check CI before it settles after a manual rerun or push. The preceding wait (`rhiza ship check --settled`) followed by its check re-evaluates the PR exactly as the change set's intent asks: a green head (or new head) continues, a still-red head gets a fresh triage. The journal records which branch led to ci-triage, so the choice is deterministic and keeps the run on the same path (pre-signoff vs post-rebase), so a post-signoff run is not sent back through signoff. One rule, built on 01M6XX4R8 instead of a special case per step, keeps run resume general.
fields.statement: A `rhiza run resume --retry` of a ship-change run that failed at ci-triage restarts at the wait step that led to the check which routed into ci-triage: wait-pr when ci-triage was reached from pr-green's on.fail, wait-rebased when reached from rebased-green's on.fail. Which one is read from the run's journal (the step visited just before ci-triage), not guessed. The run then waits for CI to settle on the current head (or a new one) and re-runs that check: green continues to signoff or land; red goes to ci-triage again with fresh state. This extends 01M6XX4R8's rule (reopen at the wait whose on.pass is the failed step) one hop: when the failed step has no such wait, follow the on.fail edge back to the step that routed into it and reopen at that step's wait.
